shape_hint: A flat, thin spring-steel washer shaped like the capital letter E: a ring open on one side with three small inward-pointing prongs (the middle one opposite the opening) that snap sideways (radially) into a shaft groove of diameter d2. Outer outline is a rounded ring of diameter d3_max, thickness s.

role_map.d2: nominal groove diameter in the shaft (also the ring size)
role_map.d1_min: smallest shaft diameter the ring is intended for
role_map.d1_max: largest shaft diameter the ring is intended for
role_map.a: opening width of the unstressed ring
role_map.d3_max: maximum outside diameter of the ring seated in the groove
role_map.n_min: minimum edge margin (groove edge to shaft end)

notes: DIN 6799 sizes the ring by GROOVE diameter d2 (E4 = 4 mm groove, shaft 5-7 mm). Korean KS B 1337 / JIS B 2804 E-rings use a different size designation and different outline dimensions (a second JIS table appears on itafasteners.com) - do not mix them with this table. Standard tolerances on s, a, d2(h11), m are not listed here. Sizes 0.8 and 30 are in the standard but rarely stocked. Current DIN 6799 edition may differ from the published tables (hint says 2026-05 edition, tables are from the older public editions).

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched fasteners.eu, beneri, woodstock, internationalsprings (www host resets, bare host 200), boltsfastener, hpceurope, westfield PDF (itafasteners probe URL 404). 18 rows x 8 cols x 7 sources compared programmatically (rowspan-split fasteners.eu cells handled by filtering tolerance cells). Only mismatches: internationalsprings E30 d1_min 30 (others 32) and E19 m 180.00 (others 1.8). Strict support count (fe, beneri, ints, hpc all cols; woodstock only s,m,n,d2; no boltsfastener, no PDF): E1.2-E24 min = 3 (cells E8 m/n, E19 m, E24 d1/a/d3), E0.8 = 2 (d1_min, d1_max, a, d3_max), E30 = 2 (d1_min). Sanity: d2<d1_min<d1_max<d3_max, a<d2, m=s+0.04..0.05, s/m/n/a/d3 non-decreasing for all kept rows.
problems: E30 d1_min=32: fasteners.eu 32, beneri 32, internationalsprings 30 (typo), westfield 32 but it is a vendor PDF -> only 2 countable clusters; the producer counted the PDF. Row E30 dropped (its other cells have exactly fe+beneri+ints, ints being the sloppy source with a duplicated part number in that row).

E0.8: beneri and hpceurope have no 0.8 row. Without boltsfastener (not counted: compilation site, caller flagged its copy behaviour) d1_min, d1_max and a have only fasteners.eu + internationalsprings; d3_max has only those two even if boltsfastener were counted (its d4 'expanded' is a different quantity), the third value comes from woodstock 'Clearance (C)' whose role is only inferred by equality with d3 in the other 15 rows. Row dropped.

Kept rows E1.2-E24 have exactly 3 clusters at E8 (m, n_min), E19 (m; ints typo 180.00), E24 (d1_min, d1_max, a, d3_max); these rest on fasteners.eu + beneri + internationalsprings being independent (beneri has own mass data; ints has own typos but uses the same Fs/Fsg symbols as fasteners.eu). Zero slack.

Role check: a = 'opening width of the unstressed ring' is defined only in the Westfield PDF key (fasteners.eu legend: 'a - opening Range'; hpceurope header 'A'); woodstock labels the same values 'Height (g)' (wrong) so it is not counted for a. d3_max: explicit 'd3 max' in beneri/ints, 'Ød3 max' in hpceurope, PDF key 'maximum external diameter when seated in the groove', fasteners.eu 'd3 - Outer diameter' -> fine. d1_min/d1_max = shaft range (legend 'd1 - shaft diameter').
woodstock 'For Shaft Diameter' column is the midpoint of d1_min/d1_max for all 16 rows it lists (checked) - consistent but not usable as min/max; woodstock has no E8 row.
boltsfastener d4 'Expanded' and mislabelled 'd3 from/to' (= d1 range) columns are not used; its a,s,m,n,d1 values equal the kept ones but it is not counted.
Size label 'E<d2>' is a trade designation (groove diameter); JIS/KS E-rings use different sizing - agreed with producer.
